title: Contact
excerpt: A wrong result, a missing calculator, a format the tools do not handle — this is the page for all three.
content:
Every message on this page is read by a person. There is no ticket robot and no autoresponder; the answer comes from whoever looked into the problem — usually the person who built the page you are writing about.

What to include

A wrong result

Name the calculator or tool, paste the values you entered, and say what answer you expected. If you know where the expected answer comes from — a textbook, a standard, a spreadsheet, a statement — say so; that turns a report into a fix. A screenshot helps when the problem is visual, but the numbers in text are what get it reproduced.

A calculator or a tool that should exist

Say what you were trying to work out and what you had in hand. "I have a room's measurements and I want paint litres by coat" is worth more than "please add a paint calculator". If it is a file format, say which tool you tried and what produced the file.

A file the tools will not open

Tell us the format, the size, and what produced it. Do not send the file itself unless we ask — the tools run in your browser and we would rather keep it that way. If we need the file to reproduce a bug we will say so, and we will tell you what to strip out of it first.

Privacy, advertising, licensing or a legal request

All of these reach the same inbox. The privacy policy, cookie policy and terms answer the usual questions first; anything about a specific record you sent us is handled through the your data and your choices page. If a copyright holder believes a page reproduces their work, say which page and what is reproduced, and it will be checked and removed if the complaint is right.

Accessibility

If a page or a tool is hard to use with a keyboard, a screen reader, a large text setting or on a small screen, describe where it breaks. Accessibility problems on a tool site are correctness problems, and they are fixed with the same priority as a wrong number.

What happens next

Bug reports are answered first, often with the fix rather than a reply — if a page changes, that is the answer arriving. Requests for new calculators are collected and built in batches, and when one you asked for goes live, that is the end of it. Anything about a particular page is answered by someone who has opened that page.

Messages are stored in the site's own database and a notification is emailed to the team. If that email fails, the message is not lost: it is kept and picked up from the panel. Messages are deleted once the question is settled, and you can ask for yours to be deleted sooner — see your data and your choices.

What we cannot do

  • Give personal advice. A message that asks "should I take this loan?" gets a pointer to how the calculator's result should be read, not a recommendation. That is not evasiveness: the site does not know your circumstances, and a few sentences by email would be read as advice.
  • Read your file. The tools never receive it. If something is wrong with a conversion, the format and a description of the problem is what makes it reproducible.
  • Recover a result you lost. Calculator values are never stored, so there is nothing on the server to recover. Re-enter the inputs and the same answer comes back.

Response times

Most messages are answered within two working days, and bug reports usually within one. There is no guaranteed response time: this is a small team, not a support desk with a service-level agreement. Messages that arrive on a weekend may wait until the start of the week.

The form

The form below asks for your name, email address, an optional phone number, a subject and your message. Those fields exist to answer you; nothing is added to a mailing list, and no message is ever used for marketing. If you would rather not use the form, the same team reads the address printed in the About page and on this page's footer.

meta_description: How to reach the team behind Onim: report a wrong result, ask for a calculator, request a file format, or ask about privacy and advertising.
